How labs make money
on blood tests

lines.text: Medicare pays $7.77 for a blood count. Labs make billions.
lines.say: Medicare pays seven seventy-seven for a blood count. Labs make billions.

lines.text: Quest Diagnostics brought in $11.04 billion in 2025.
lines.say: Quest Diagnostics brought in about eleven billion dollars in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: The trick is volume: about 244 million orders that year.
lines.say: The trick is volume: about two hundred forty-four million orders that year.

lines.text: Our math: $10.79B in testing revenue divided by those orders is about $44 each.
lines.say: Our math: about ten point eight billion in testing revenue, divided by those orders, is about forty-four dollars each.

lines.text: Quest says an order's value depends on how many tests, which tests, and who pays.
lines.say: Quest says an order's value depends on how many tests, which tests, and who pays.

lines.text: Medicare pays one national price, while private insurers negotiate their own rates.
lines.say: Medicare pays one national price, while private insurers negotiate their own rates.

lines.text: Revenue fell from $10.79B in 2021 to $9.25B in 2023 as COVID testing faded.
lines.say: Revenue fell from about ten point eight billion in twenty twenty-one to about nine point two five billion in twenty twenty-three as COVID testing faded.

lines.text: That's about a 14% drop, before more orders pushed it past its old high.
lines.say: That's about a fourteen percent drop, before more orders pushed it past its old high.

lines.text: So a lab isn't selling one pricey test. It's selling millions of cheap ones.

post.title: Medicare pays $7.77 for a blood count. How do labs profit?
post.ig:
Medicare pays $7.77 for a basic blood count. So how do labs make billions?
Quest Diagnostics brought in $11.04 billion in 2025.
It handled about 244 million test orders. Our math: about $44 in testing revenue per order.
The price depends on the tests in each order and who pays: Medicare sets one national rate, insurers negotiate.
Sources: Quest Diagnostics FY2025 results and annual report, CMS Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule.
News and education, not financial advice.
